instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Bring 3 cups of water and 1 tsp of the salt to a boil in a medium pot.
Meanwhile, trim the zucchini and halve them lengthwise. Scoop out the middle of each half with a spoon, leaving a wall about 1/2 inch thick. Finely chop the scooped pulp.
Add the rice to the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes. Add the chopped pulp and cook for 5 minutes. Drain well. The rice will still be firm, and it finishes in the oven.

While the rice cooks, mince the garlic. In a 9 by 13 inch baking dish, stir together 2 cups of the passata, the garlic, the oil, 1/4 tsp of the salt, the pepper and 6 torn basil leaves. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Set the zucchini halves in the sauce, cut side up. Dice the fontina into 8 cubes. Grate the Grana Padano. That should be about 1/2 cup.
Stir the butter and Grana Padano into the drained rice, with 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Fill each zucchini half about halfway with rice. Press a cube of fontina into each, then cover with the rest of the rice, mounding it a little.
Bake for 22 minutes, until a knife slides into the zucchini easily and the rice is golden at the edges.
Scatter the remaining basil over the top. Serve the zucchini with the sauce from the dish spooned over.
method_notes: The Ligurian lead cooks Carnaroli rice with the zucchini pulp, stirs in butter and Grana Padano, hides a cube of fontina in each boat and cooks them in tomato sauce. The other version bakes halved boats with a rice and mozzarella filling at 425°F. This one takes the oven route to fit 50 minutes: the rice is only part-cooked first, and the boats bake in the sauce.
